newsitem.title: USA: SAFECO to acquire American States - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: SAFECO to acquire American States - WSJ.

text.p: SAFECO Corp is expected to announce later today that it has an agreement to acquire American States Financial Corp for $2.82 billion, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal cited unnamed sources familiar with the matter as saying the transaction represents a $47-a-share price.
The acquisition would combine SAFECO, a large West Coast property-casualty insurer, with a unit of Lincoln National Corp, which owns 83 percent of American States.
In addition to $2.35 billion Lincoln would receive for its 50 million shares, the Indiana-based insurance concern would receive $300 million to cover loans it has outstanding to American States.
SAFECO also will pay $470 million for the shares owned by the public, the Journal said.
There had been rumors in the past several weeks that a deal for American States was set to be announced.

Top contenders for the commercial property-casualty business were believed to include Hartford Financial Services Group Inc, Travelers Property Casualty Corp, Germany's Allianz AG Holding, and the U.K.'s General Accident Plc.
SAFECO believes the transaction would have a neutral effet on per-share earnings in the first year and would add to earnings thereafter, the Journal said.

The deal, which is subject to regulatory review and approval, is expected to close in three to four months. SAFECO plans to finance the deal with $600 million of internal funds, $700 million by issuing common stock and $1.8 billion from preferred stock and bank debt, the Journal said.
